column4: dialect-gated per SUBTEST: one arm per dialect, each calling testutil.TestDB, so mysql and mssql skip in these PostgreSQL-only jobs while postgres RUNS -- two, not three. Measured by name rather than by delta, with CLEAT_TEST_MYSQL and CLEAT_TEST_MSSQL unset: go test ./engine/testutil/ -run TestForeignSessionsSeesAnotherProcess -count=1 -json | grep '"Action":"skip"' reports exactly TestForeignSessionsSeesAnotherProcess/mysql and /mssql, with /postgres passing. The arms have to exist even where they skip, because the thing under test is THREE DIFFERENT QUERIES against three different system views -- pg_stat_activity, information_schema.PROCESSLIST joined to session_connect_attrs, and sys.dm_exec_sessions -- and each identifies the client process a different way (a tagged application_name, _pid, host_process_id). A postgres-only run cannot vouch for either of the other two. This is the cleat#982 probe, whose whole purpose is that an empty foreign-session list must MEAN something; a dialect arm that silently returned nothing would report the reassuring answer forever, which is the exact failure the test is a control for.
